KASPER BACKPACK - CARRIER FOR WAVESHARE ESP32-S3-TOUCH-LCD-4.3B
BUILD, WIRING, POWER AND SERVICE NOTES
- Firmware, docs, unit tests, UI simulator: https://github.com/bckasper3/WaveShare4.3
- 3D-printable stand / bench holder for the Waveshare 4.3":
- REV-9: latest design, not built yet. Drawn before the REV-8 bring-up findings.
- Desktop case rev A (wedge, screen tilted 30 deg) is sized for REV-9.
- BOM_*.xlsx + PickAndPlace_*.xlsx = JLCPCB assembly (LCSC part numbers).
- 3D_*.step = assembled board model. SCH_*.pdf = schematic. PCB_*.pdf = all layers.
- FlyingProbeTesting.json inside the Gerber zip is the authoritative pad-to-net map.
- REV-8: H10/H11 swap was made after the schematic export. Trust the PCB netlist.
- 1S1P Li-ion/LiPo ONLY: 3.7 V nominal, 4.2 V full. JST-PH 2.0 mm lead.
Hobby leads are not standardized: CHECK POLARITY WITH A METER.
A reversed cell destroys the TP4056 charger.
- U4 (battery) and U7 (rocker) are the SAME connector type. Check before plugging in.
- Use a PROTECTED pack (PCM, cutoff ~2.5-3.0 V, a few amps). The board has no
- Mount on the flat back with zip ties through the slots. Foam pad or Kapton between
cell and PCB. Snug, not crushing.
- Do not store flat: a protected cell left at cutoff for months may refuse to charge.
- After connecting or reconnecting the battery: switch the rocker ON, then OFF, once.
- USB-C 5 V (front, U8 TUSB320 CC controller).
- 12 V barrel jack 5.5 x 2.1 mm (F1, D1).
- 12 V inputs: fused, Schottky diode-OR'd, TVS-clamped (D3), AP63205 buck (U1) to 5V_DC.
5V_DC joins USB VBUS on 5V_IN through D4. Reverse polarity is blocked.
- SYS: ~3.0 V (flat cell) to ~4.7 V (external power through D5).
- Boost converter (U9/L3) makes a steady 5.1 V for the Waveshare in every mode.
- 3V3_AON: small LDO (U6), always on: INA219 + TUSB320.
- TP4056 (U3), 600 mA (set by R13), CC/CV to 4.20 V.
- ~4 h for a 2000 mAh cell from empty. Works with the rocker on or off.
- CHG_EN (TP4056 CE) pulled up by R14 = charging enabled by default.
Waveshare DO0 ON = charging DISABLED (firmware uses it for weak USB sources).
- From a PC port: 4.71 V at the connector, 4.26 V on 5V_IN (Q6 + D8 drop),
so the last part of the charge is slow.
- 5 V to a flash drive, TPS2041B current limit (~0.5 A continuous).
POWER DRAW (measured on REV-8 unless noted)
- Screen on: ~570 mA from the cell (~550 mA at 5 V).
- Boost input peaks: ~1.4-1.8 A from a 3.4 V cell.
- Rocker off, standby: ~175 uA (about 1.3 years on 2000 mAh).
- Rocker off right after a battery reconnect: ~800 uA (about 3-4 months)
until the rocker is switched on and off once (INA219 powers up in continuous mode,
~0.7 mA; firmware puts it into power-down at every boot).
- Standby budget: AP2112K LDO ~55 uA, INA219 power-down ~6 uA, TUSB320 CC watch,
- Runtime, 2000 mAh, screen at full brightness: ~2.5-3 h (estimate).
3000 mAh: ~1.5x. Longer with backlight dimming and idle timeout.
- No battery connected: TP4056 cycles to 4.2 V and back (LED2 flickers).
Firmware shows battery level as "--" in that case.
- Meter on uA in the battery lead, with a JUMPER ACROSS THE METER.
- Rocker on ~15 s, rocker off, remove jumper, read.
- Refit the jumper before touching the rocker or the meter leads. Changing jacks or
ranges breaks the circuit, resets the INA219 and reads ~800 uA. It also protects the
uA fuse from the 570 mA boot current.
- Waveshare 16-pin terminal to carrier headers H8-H11, pin for pin.
- DO NOT WIRE TERMINAL PINS 7 AND 8 (CAN L / CAN H). They couple noise onto I2C
and make the screen blink. Do not use H3's CAN pins with them connected either.
- Waveshare VOUT (terminal pin 3) = 3.3 V. Measure H8-3. Never 5 V: it feeds the
I2C pull-up position and would over-drive the TUSB320 (rated 3.6 V).
- Waveshare SW2 (CAN / RS-485 120 R termination) = OFF (factory default).
- Keep jumper wires short and away from the boost converter (L3/U9).
- Long I2C wires (terminal 5/6): twist each with a ground wire.
- Waveshare USB-C to the ESP32 (D+/D- on GPIO19/20). Flash firmware through it.
I2C BUS (GPIO8 SDA / GPIO9 SCL, shared, 3.3 V)
0x40 INA219 (U5) 0x41 TMR probe ADS122C04 (A0 to DVDD)
- Terminal SDA/SCL go through a MOSFET level shifter, 4.7k to VOUT.
- RS-485: Waveshare auto-direction transceiver (UART0, GPIO43/44), Modbus RTU slave.
560 R failsafe bias. 120 R termination is DNP (R28 + R30).
- DO1: open drain, 5-36 V, 450 mA. DI0/DI1: Waveshare optocoupled inputs.
- I/O NOT ISOLATED: Waveshare I/O ground is tied to board GND at H11-2.
- LED1 yellow (NCD0603Y2) = external power present -> LP1
- LED3 green (KT-0603G) = rocker on, powered -> LP3
- LP1-LP3: Bivar SLP3-150-100-F (3 mm, flat lens, right-angle, press-fit).
NOT IN THE BOM: order separately, fit by hand.
- Check LED4 orientation against the cathode mark during assembly.
- Faint LED1 with nothing plugged in = ESP32 D+ pull-up leaking through D7's VBUS
steering diode (~1 mA). Fixed in firmware (pull-up only while a cable is attached).
- Built REV-8 boards have a TUSB320L (I2C 0x47). Firmware accepts both.
- Keep the BOM and the assembly order in agreement.
- Default USB role is device (PC). Host (flash drive) only when U8 reports a drive.
- R4, R5 5.1k C27834 CC1/CC2 to GND. ONLY if U8 is NOT fitted.
- R7 100k C149504 5V_OUT to SRC_EN_N: holds TPS2041B off, no host mode.
- R20 0R C17477 PWR_SW_G to GND: bypasses the rocker, always on.
- R24, R25 10k C17414 Extra I2C pull-ups to WS_VOUT. Long leads / slow edges.
- R27 0R C17477 12V_IN to SENS_SEL: sensor powered from 12 V, not 5 V.
- R28 + R30 0R + 120R RS-485 termination, in series through TERM_B.
Only if this unit is always at the physical end of the bus.
UPDI, SDA, SCL, SENS_PWR, GND. Hand-fit.
- H4 Power test: 12V_IN, 5V_DC, VBUS_EXT, VBUS_SINK, 5V_IN, BAT_NODE, SYS, SYS_SW
- H5 Signal test: 5V_OUT, 3V3_AON, SDA, SCL, USB_ID, SENS_PWR, WS_VOUT, CHG_EN
- REV-8 only: H7 UPDI (program the sensor AVR), H12 SENS_PWR test point,
Fitted by default: H3 expansion (SYS, 5V_OUT, 3V3_AON, SDA, SCL, CANH, CANL, GND),
H8-H11 Waveshare terminal headers, R6, R26.
- All SMD parts on the top side. Back is flat for the battery.
- Hand-solder through-hole: DB9 (DB1), barrel jack, JST-PH battery (U4) and
rocker (U7) headers, light pipes, any optional headers.
- Power traces: use pours for anything over ~300 mA, several vias per amp
1. No battery, no Waveshare. 12 V on the barrel jack, supply limited to 200 mA.
2. Fit a rocker (or short U7). Check SYS_SW on H4, 5V_OUT = 5.1 V on H5. LED3 lights.
3. Bench supply 3.7 V / 1 A limit on U4 (pin 1 = +). Charge current flows, LED4 lights.
4. Front USB-C to a PC: charges. Flash drive in: 5 V on VBUS.
5. Connect the Waveshare (no CAN L/H), flash firmware, I2C scan:
6. Rocker on, then off. Standby ~175 uA (jumper method above).
- U8 part differs between BOM and built boards (see above).
- DNP parts are not marked "DNP" on the schematic (hidden BOM flag only).
- INA219 on the always-on rail: a battery reconnect leaves ~800 uA standby until
the next boot. Option: move it to the switched rail.
- AP2112K (~55 uA) for 3V3_AON: a ~1 uA-Iq LDO would bring standby to ~50-100 uA.
- D7 ESD array: choose one without a VBUS rail.
- Q6 + D8 drop slows the end of charge from a PC port: consider an ideal diode.
- No RTC backup cell on the Waveshare as built: the clock resets with power.
